gloss: to get along well; to hit it off; to be compatible

definitions.gloss: to get along well; to hit it off; to be compatible
definitions.explanation: to have a natural affinity or compatibility with someone, sharing similar tastes, interests, or temperament

examples.japanese: あの{二人|ふたり}は{気|き}が{合|あ}う。
{初|はじ}めて{会|あ}ったのに、すぐ{気|き}が{合|あ}った。
examples.english: Even though we met for the first time, we hit it off right away.

examples.japanese: {趣味|しゅみ}が{同|おな}じだから、{彼|かれ}とは{気|き}が{合|あ}うのかもしれない。
examples.english: Maybe I get along with him because we have the same hobbies.

notes:
An idiomatic expression using {気|き} (spirit, feeling, temperament) and {合|あ}う (to match, to fit). Describes a natural compatibility between people — a sense that personalities, interests, or values align well.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {人|ひと}と{気|き}が{合|あ}う: to get along with someone
- {気|き}が{合|あ}う{仲間|なかま}: like-minded companions
- {気|き}が{合|あ}う{友達|ともだち}: a friend you click with

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {馬|うま}が{合|あ}う: to hit it off — similar meaning but slightly more casual; literally "the horses match"
- {相性|あいしょう}がいい: to be compatible — broader, also used for romantic compatibility and object compatibility
- {気|き}が{合|あ}わない: to not get along — the negative form, used when personalities clash

USAGE:
Typically used with the particle と to indicate the person one gets along with. The subject is often implied rather than stated explicitly.
